post.text:
A guy tested almost every AI mini PC so you don't have to.

What surprised me is that they all had the same AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 chip and 128GB of memory.

On paper, they should've been nearly identical.

They weren't.

The biggest differences came from things most people ignore:

→ Dual 10Gb Ethernet
→ USB4 V2 (80 Gbit/s)
→ PCIe expansion
→ Memory configuration

The wildest part?

Just changing how the memory was allocated improved AI performance by up to 15% on the exact same hardware.

No new chip.
No overclocking.
Just better configuration.

That tells you where we're headed.

AI hardware is becoming interchangeable.

The companies that win won't necessarily have the fastest chip, they'll have the best software, the smartest engineering, and the strongest ecosystem.

We're moving into a different kind of AI hardware race.
